requirements.text: Update the existing entitlement for their Palo Alto Networks PA-3220 Variant 8 to our highest Enterprise support level
requirements.sql: SELECT COUNT(*) FROM entitlement WHERE entitlement_id = 73 AND support_level = 'enterprise'
assumptions: Stark Industries is account 8; Palo Alto Networks PA-3220 Variant 8 is product 140
entitlement 73 is the account's only entitlement for product 140 (active, under active contract 22)
the highest support level in the policy's list is enterprise

requirements.sql: SELECT COUNT(*) FROM entitlement WHERE entitlement_id = 73 AND coverage_hours = 'h24x7'
assumptions: 24x7 coverage is the coverage_hours value h24x7

requirements.sql: SELECT COUNT(*) FROM entitlement WHERE entitlement_id = 73 AND max_cases_per_month = 0
assumptions: the policy reads max_cases_per_month = 0 as unlimited; the seed value is 10

requirements.text: Update the existing entitlement for their Palo Alto Networks PA-3220 Variant 8
requirements.selector: account_id = 8 AND product_id IS NULL AND active = 1
requirements.sql: SELECT COUNT(*) FROM entitlement WHERE account_id = 8 AND product_id IS NULL AND active = 1 AND support_level = 'premium' AND coverage_hours = 'h12x6'
assumptions: entitlements 68 and 71 are the account's active account-wide entitlements, which also cover the device; the request names the product-specific entitlement only, so they keep their support level and coverage

requirements.text: Register a new critical case for this device, reporting that the Dataplane crashes repeatedly, using the phone channel
requirements.sql: SELECT COUNT(*) FROM customer_case WHERE case_id = 1233 AND account_id = 8 AND contact_id = 10 AND product_id = 140 AND installed_product_id = 42 AND priority = 'critical' AND channel = 'phone'
assumptions: id assumed next in sequence (highest case_id is 1232)
Marc Henry is portal user 20, contact 10 of Stark Industries (account 8), taken as the reporting contact
this device is installed product 42, the account's only installed product of product 140 (in_use)

disagreement: product_id: A 140, B untested; chose 140 because the policy requires the installed product's product to match the case product, and all 737 seed cases with an installed product carry that product's id

requirements.text: reporting that the Dataplane crashes repeatedly
requirements.sql: SELECT COUNT(*) FROM customer_case WHERE case_id = 1233 AND short_description LIKE '%dataplane%' AND short_description LIKE '%crash%'
assumptions: id assumed next in sequence (highest case_id is 1232)
the reported issue must appear in the short description; only the request's own words are tested, not the policy's description template

requirements.text: Assign the case to Curtis McCoy
requirements.sql: SELECT COUNT(*) FROM customer_case WHERE case_id = 1233 AND assigned_to = 177
assumptions: id assumed next in sequence (highest case_id is 1232)
Curtis McCoy is user 177 (Curtis Mccoy), an active manager and already a member of Escalation Management (group 18), so no membership is added

requirements.sql: SELECT COUNT(*) FROM customer_case WHERE case_id = 1233 AND assignment_group_id = 18
assumptions: id assumed next in sequence (highest case_id is 1232)
Escalation Management is group 18 by exact name; groups 38, 58 and 78 carry numbered suffixes

requirements.text: Assign the case to Curtis McCoy and the Escalation Management group
requirements.sql: SELECT COUNT(*) FROM customer_case WHERE case_id = 1233 AND state = 'in_progress'
assumptions: id assumed next in sequence (highest case_id is 1232)
the policy sets a new case to in_progress when it is assigned to a group or user, and requires in_progress before an SLA is linked

requirements.text: Ensure the mandatory Resolution SLA is applied to this case
requirements.sql: SELECT COUNT(*) FROM case_sla WHERE case_id = 1233 AND sla_def_id = 6 AND stage = 'in_progress'
assumptions: the resolution SLA for a critical case is SLA Resolution - Critical (sla_def_id 6), active; the global resolution SLA (10) is inactive
the policy sets the linked SLA's stage to in_progress so tracking starts at once

disagreement: anchor: A case_sla_id 2465, B selector case_id 1233 AND sla_def_id 6; chose the selector because every seed case carries two SLA rows and the policy aligns an SLA when a case moves to in progress, so a response SLA may be linked first and the resolution row's place in the sequence is not fixed; the benchmark's checks also name the row by case and definition

requirements.text: Register a new critical case for this device
requirements.sql: SELECT COUNT(*) FROM interaction WHERE interaction_id = 1233 AND case_id = 1233 AND account_id = 8 AND contact_id = 10 AND channel = 'phone'
assumptions: id assumed next in sequence (highest interaction_id is 1232)
the policy makes an interaction mandatory whenever a new case is registered
every seed interaction carries its case's channel, account and contact, so the new one carries phone, account 8 and contact 10
no tool writes this table by name; create_new_case may write it with the case

update_entitlement (3).evidence: tests only that entitlement 73 has a non-null sys_updated_on, a server-kept timestamp already set on the seed (2026-06-20 20:33:07), so it holds before the agent acts

notes:
No acting user is given, so the policy's default administrator role applies, which may update entitlements; Marc Henry is the customer contact reporting the issue.
The interaction row is required by the policy rather than the request and no listed tool names interactions, so it may fail unless case creation adds one itself.
The policy's short-description template is not tested; only the request's report of dataplane crashes is.
Only the resolution SLA is required; the request does not ask for the response SLA. Escalation is not requested and is not tested.
The benchmark's checks are written as value queries; each is carried here as a count query on the same row.
disagreement: missing requirement: a stay that Stark Industries' active account-wide entitlements (68 and 71) keep support level premium and coverage h12x6: one pass wrote it, the other did not; kept because both also cover the device, so a loose reading of 'the existing entitlement for their' device would sweep them in, which is the selector boundary a stay records.
disagreement: the short-description cells (dataplane and crash) sit inside the case-creation requirement in one pass and form their own new requirement in the other; kept as their own requirement because the benchmark tests no description, so its case-creation checks stay separable from the added cells; the case of 'Dataplane' does not matter, since LIKE ignores ASCII case.
disagreement: the assignment is one requirement (user and group) in one pass and two in the other; kept as two, one per benchmark check, since the request names the user and the group separately and each can fail on its own.
disagreement: product_id 140 on the new case: tested in one pass, untested in the other; kept, as recorded on the case-creation requirement.
disagreement: the resolution SLA row anchored to the next case_sla_id in one pass and selected by case and SLA definition in the other; chose the selector, as recorded on the SLA requirement.
